text.p: Israeli troops wounded 130 Palestinians, seven seriously, during a stone-throwing protest on Wednesday against Israeli policy on Jerusalem, the director of Ramallah hospital said.
Director Shawqi Harb said most of the Palestinians treated had wounds from rubber bullets although one was wounded by gunfire from an M-16 rifle and some suffered from teargas inhalation.
He corrected reports by hospital sources that one protester, Yasser Abed al-Ghani, 23, of Tulkarm in the West Bank, had died. The director said Ghani was critically wounded and in surgery.
"Until now we have treated 130, mostly from rubber bullet wounds. This number is changing fast. We have just admitted someone wounded by an M-16," Harb told Reuters.
He said seven were in critical condition. All were wounded during a demonstration on the outskirts of Ramallah, north of Jerusalem. Palestinians crowded into the hospital to donate blood.
"It's a fluid situation. Five are in critical condition. They are in surgery now," he said. "I think we will be getting more wounded by the M-16."

Palestinians in Jerusalem and across the West Bank and Gaza Strip answered a call by Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority to demonstrate against Israel's opening of a tunnel near an Islamic shrine in Jerusalem's walled Old City.
Acting Israeli Prime Minister Moshe Katzav said the government was working to calm the atmosphere.

Katzav, acting in the absence of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on a trip to Europe, told army radio: "There were contacts during the day with the Palaestinian Authority on both the governmental and official levels.
"I hope that the explanations I gave them and that our officials gave the Waqf (Islamic Trust) officials will cause them to reduce their efforts to inflame the atmosphere."
